title: Overlay status feed messages
description: JSON status events the orchestrator broadcasts over a localhost-only socket for the Teleprompter overlay to render (spec/00 D13/D19, Contract P). Transport is one JSON object per line (NDJSON) on 127.0.0.1. The overlay is a dumb subscriber: it renders whatever arrives and never drives the voice loop. Protocol: receivers ignore unknown message types (log once); every message carries 'type'. The 'state' values are the overlay's own; its listening indicator inherits spec/50's truthful-indicator rule (shows 'listening' only while audio is actually being captured).

state.description: orchestrator->overlay: coarse session state — drives the island's mode (idle = asleep/hidden, listening = bars, thinking = processing, speaking = reply shown, error = fault). 'listening' also covers the follow-up window (mic open, spec/40).

transcript.description: orchestrator->overlay: the user's transcribed prompt AFTER the deterministic word-replacement/cleanup (spec/40, D15). 'final':false is reserved for streaming STT (deferred); M0 always sends final:true. The overlay accumulates finals for the expandable session history (D14, in-memory).

response.description: orchestrator->overlay: one chunk of the brain's reply as it streams (the teleprompter, D14). The overlay appends 'delta' to the current reply; 'done':true marks the reply complete. Clearing: a 'state' that starts a new turn ('listening', 'thinking') or ends the session ('idle') clears the reply and any fault; 'speaking' and 'error' deliberately do NOT — the reply streams in during THINKING and the island flips to SPEAKING while it is read, so clearing there would blank the text exactly as the user starts reading it.

mic.description: orchestrator->overlay: mic input level in [0,1], emitted while a capture window is open (LISTENING / FOLLOW-UP) — drives the listening bars and is the spec/50 truthful indicator for those windows: whenever a capture window is open a 'mic' message is present, and the overlay must not infer 'listening' from anything else. Always-on-mic monitoring — the wake-word watch at IDLE and barge-in detection during SPEAKING — is a separate, user-gated category that deliberately emits no 'mic' (both are governed together by the 'listen for me' setting, spec/70); so the island shows no mic cue while Gemma speaks. High-frequency and droppable.

latency.description: orchestrator->overlay: a per-turn latency reading as the orchestrator measures it against the spec/40 targets. 'feedback' = end-of-speech -> first perceptible feedback; 'first_word' = end-of-speech -> first spoken word. Instrument data for the M0 acceptance run, not user-facing chrome by default.

error.description: orchestrator->overlay: why the current turn failed. Pairs with a state:'error' message (which flips the island to its fault mode); this carries the human-facing reason so the surface can explain the fault, not merely flag it. 'kind' is the Contract-B error taxonomy (spec/20: auth | rate_limit | context | unavailable | malformed_tool_call | unknown) carried as a free string for styling/affordances — receivers tolerate unknown kinds. 'message' is the one-line explanation (the same sentence spoken per spec/40 narration).
